pp:ce:2026:q16.solution_markdown: Given: Bag I: 4 white + 6 black = 10 balls Bag II: 4 white + 3 black = 7 balls Using Bayes' Theorem: Let B = event of drawing a black ball Let $B_1$ = Bag I chosen, $B_2$ = Bag II chosen $P(B_1) = P(B_2) = \dfrac{1}{2}$ (equal probability of choosing either bag) $P(B | B_1) = \dfrac{6}{10} = 0.6$ $P(B | B_2) = \dfrac{3}{7} \approx 0.4286$ Total probability of black ball: $P(B) = P(B_1) \cdot P(B|B_1) + P(B_2) \cdot P(B|B_2)$ $P(B) = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{6}{10} + \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{3}{7} = \dfrac{3}{10} + \dfrac{3}{14} = \dfrac{21}{70} + \dfrac{15}{70} = \dfrac{36}{70}$ Probability black ball came from Bag I: $P(B_1|B) = \dfrac{P(B_1) \cdot P(B|B_1)}{P(B)} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{6}{10}}{\dfrac{36}{70}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{3}{10}}{\dfrac{36}{70}} = \dfrac{3}{10} \times \dfrac{70}{36} = \dfrac{210}{360} = \dfrac{7}{12} \approx \mathbf{0.58}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **0.58** (acceptable range: [0.5, 0.66]).

pp:ce:2026:q17.solution_markdown: Given matrix: $$A = \begin{bmatrix} 9 & 15 \\ 15 & 50 \end{bmatrix}$$ Cholesky decomposition: $A = LL^T$, where $$L = \begin{bmatrix} l_{11} & 0 \\ l_{21} & l_{22} \end{bmatrix}$$ Step 1 - Find $l_{11}$: $l_{11} = \sqrt{a_{11}} = \sqrt{9} = 3$ Step 2 - Find $l_{21}$: $l_{21} = \dfrac{a_{21}}{l_{11}} = \dfrac{15}{3} = 5$ Step 3 - Find $l_{22}$: $l_{22} = \sqrt{a_{22} - l_{21}^2} = \sqrt{50 - 25} = \sqrt{25} = 5$ $|l_{22}| = \mathbf{5}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **5**.

pp:ce:2026:q18.solution_markdown: Given: $(x + y - 7)^2 + (y + 3x - 13)^2 = 0$ Key insight: Sum of two squares equals zero only when each square is zero. $(x + y - 7)^2 = 0 \Rightarrow x + y = 7 \quad \cdots (1)$ $(y + 3x - 13)^2 = 0 \Rightarrow y + 3x = 13 \quad \cdots (2)$ Solving the system: Subtract (1) from (2): $(y + 3x) - (x + y) = 13 - 7$ $2x = 6 \Rightarrow x = 3$ Substitute into (1): $3 + y = 7 \Rightarrow y = 4$ Calculate $x^3 + y^3 = 3^3 + 4^3 = 27 + 64 = \mathbf{91}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **91**.

pp:ce:2026:q19.concept_summary: RCC Structures - Footing, Columns, Beams and Slabs
pp:ce:2026:q19.solution_markdown: Concept: The area of steel per unit width must remain the same to resist the same design moment. Given: 10 mm bars at spacing $s_1 = 150$ mm 12 mm bars at spacing $s_2 = ?$ Area of steel per unit width must be equal: $\dfrac{A_{st1}}{s_1} = \dfrac{A_{st2}}{s_2}$ $\dfrac{\pi/4 \times 10^2}{150} = \dfrac{\pi/4 \times 12^2}{s_2}$ $s_2 = 150 \times \dfrac{12^2}{10^2} = 150 \times \dfrac{144}{100} = 150 \times 1.44 = \mathbf{216 \text{ mm}}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **216** (acceptable range: [214, 218]).

pp:ce:2026:q20.concept_summary: Design of Steel Structures - Structural Fasteners
pp:ce:2026:q20.solution_markdown: Concept: The design strength of a fillet weld = weld size x throat factor x length x weld strength. For the same load, the product (size x length) must remain constant. Given: Original: size $s_1 = 5$ mm, length $L_1 = 150$ mm New: size $s_2 = 6$ mm, length $L_2 = ?$ Equating weld capacity: $s_1 \times L_1 = s_2 \times L_2$ $5 \times 150 = 6 \times L_2$ $L_2 = \dfrac{750}{6} = \mathbf{125 \text{ mm}}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **125** (acceptable range: [120, 130]).

pp:ce:2026:q21.concept_summary: Geotechnical Engineering - Effective Stress and Permeability
pp:ce:2026:q21.solution_markdown: Given: Permeability corresponding to void ratio $e_1=0.60$ is $k_1=0.14\ \text{cm/s}$ The required void ratio is $e_2=0.80$ Using Taylor's equation for permeability: $k \propto \dfrac{e^3}{1+e}$ Therefore, $\dfrac{k_2}{k_1} = \frac{\dfrac{e_2^3}{1+e_2}} {\dfrac{e_1^3}{1+e_1}}$ Substituting the given values: $$\begin{aligned} k_2 &=0.14\left(\dfrac{\dfrac{(0.80)^3}{1+0.80}} {\dfrac{(0.60)^3}{1+0.60}}\right)\\[4pt] &=0.14\left(\dfrac{\dfrac{0.512}{1.8}} {\dfrac{0.216}{1.6}}\right)\\[4pt] &=0.14\left(\dfrac{0.2844}{0.135}\right)\\[4pt] &=0.14(2.107)\\ &=0.295 \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **0.3** (acceptable range: [0.28, 0.32]).

pp:ce:2026:q22.concept_summary: Geotechnical Engineering - Soil Stabilization and Soil Exploration
pp:ce:2026:q22.solution_markdown: Area Ratio formula: $A_r = \dfrac{D_e^2 - D_i^2}{D_i^2} \times 100\%$ Given, $A_r = 10\%$, $D_e = 50.8$ mm, Solving for $D_i$ $0.10 = \dfrac{50.8^2 - D_i^2}{D_i^2}$ $0.10 \cdot D_i^2 = 50.8^2 - D_i^2$ $1.10 \cdot D_i^2 = 50.8^2 = 2580.64$ $D_i^2 = \dfrac{2580.64}{1.10} = 2346.04$ $D_i = \sqrt{2346.04} = \mathbf{48.4 \text{ mm}}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **48.4** (acceptable range: [48.2, 48.6]).

pp:ce:2026:q23.solution_markdown: Space Mean Speed (SMS) is the harmonic mean of individual speeds. Given: Distance = 2 km, Travel times = 4, 5, 8 minutes Step 1 - Individual speeds: $v_1 = \dfrac{2 \text{ km}}{4/60 \text{ h}} = 30 \text{ km/h}$ $v_2 = \dfrac{2}{5/60} = 24 \text{ km/h}$ $v_3 = \dfrac{2}{8/60} = 15 \text{ km/h}$ Step 2 - Space Mean Speed (harmonic mean): $SMS = \dfrac{n}{\sum \dfrac{1}{v_i}} = \dfrac{3}{\dfrac{1}{30} + \dfrac{1}{24} + \dfrac{1}{15}}$ $= \dfrac{3}{\dfrac{4}{120} + \dfrac{5}{120} + \dfrac{8}{120}} = \dfrac{3}{\dfrac{17}{120}} = \dfrac{3 \times 120}{17} = \dfrac{360}{17} = \mathbf{21.18 \text{ km/h}}$ Alternatively: $SMS = \dfrac{\text{Total distance}}{\text{Average travel time}} = \dfrac{2}{(4+5+8)/(3 \times 60)} = \dfrac{2 \times 3 \times 60}{17} = \dfrac{360}{17} \approx \mathbf{21.18 \text{ km/h}}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **20.95** (acceptable range: [20, 21.9]).

pp:ce:2026:q24.concept_summary: Geomatics Engineering - Fundamental Concepts of Surveying
pp:ce:2026:q24.solution_markdown: Correction due to temperature change: $C_T = \alpha \cdot (T_m - T_s) \cdot L$ Given: $\alpha = 11 \times 10^{-6}$ per $^\circ C$ $T_m = 35 ^\circ C$ (measurement temperature) $T_s = 25^\circ C$ (standard temperature) $L = 200$ m (measured length) Calculation: $C_T = 11 \times 10^{-6} \times (35 - 25) \times 200$ $C_T = 11 \times 10^{-6} \times 10 \times 200$ $C_T = 11 \times 10^{-6} \times 2000$ $C_T = 0.022 \text{ m} = \mathbf{22 \text{ mm}}$ Note: Since temperature increased, the tape expanded, so the actual length is slightly more than measured. The correction is positive (+22 mm). Therefore, the correct answer is **22**.

pp:ce:2026:q25.solution_markdown: Given: Height of Plane of Collimation (HPC) = 100.000 m Back Sight (BS) on staff at point P = 1.500 m Concept: $\text{HPC} = \text{RL of P} + \text{BS}$ Therefore: $\text{RL of P} = \text{HPC} - \text{BS}$ $\text{RL of P} = 100.000 - 1.500 = \mathbf{98.500 \text{ m}}$ Explanation: The staff reading (back sight) is taken at a known/benchmark point. The HPC is height of the instrument line of sight. The RL of P is obtained by subtracting the staff reading from the HPC. Therefore, the correct answer is **98.5**.

pp:ce:2026:q26.solution_markdown: Given: $\int_0^2 f(x)[x - f(x)]\,dx = \dfrac{2}{3}$ Expand the integrand: $\int_0^2 x \cdot f(x)\,dx - \int_0^2 [f(x)]^2\,dx = \dfrac{2}{3}$ Rearrange using completing the square: $-\int_0^2 \left[f(x) - \dfrac{x}{2}\right]^2 dx + \int_0^2 \dfrac{x^2}{4}\,dx = \dfrac{2}{3}$ Evaluate $\int_0^2 \dfrac{x^2}{4}\,dx$: $= \dfrac{1}{4} \cdot \dfrac{x^3}{3}\Big|_0^2 = \dfrac{1}{4} \cdot \dfrac{8}{3} = \dfrac{2}{3}$ Substituting: $-\int_0^2 \left[f(x) - \dfrac{x}{2}\right]^2 dx + \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{2}{3}$ $\int_0^2 \left[f(x) - \dfrac{x}{2}\right]^2 dx = 0$ Since the integrand is non-negative and continuous: $f(x) = \dfrac{x}{2} \text{ for all } x \in [0, 2]$ $f(1) = \dfrac{1}{2}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

pp:ce:2026:q27.solution_markdown: Given ODE: $x^2 \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 6y$ $\rightarrow$ $x^2 y'' - 6y = 0$ This is an Euler-Cauchy equation. Assume $y = x^m$: $y' = mx^{m-1},\quad y'' = m(m-1)x^{m-2}$ Substituting: $x^2 \cdot m(m-1)x^{m-2} - 6x^m = 0$ $m(m-1)x^m - 6x^m = 0$ $[m(m-1) - 6]x^m = 0$ $m^2 - m - 6 = 0$ $(m-3)(m+2) = 0$ $m = 3 \text{ or } m = -2$ General solution: $y(x) = ax^3 + bx^{-2} = ax^3 + \dfrac{b}{x^2}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ce:2026:q28.solution_markdown: Setup: Members PQ and QR, each inclined at 45$^\circ$, hinge supports at P and R, free DOFs at Q: u (horizontal) and v (vertical). Member PQ: inclined at 135$^\circ$ from positive x-axis (going up-left from Q to P) Direction cosines: $l = \cos 135 ^\circ = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$, $m = \sin 135 ^\circ = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ Stiffness contribution at Q from PQ: $$k_{PQ} = \dfrac{AE}{L}\begin{bmatrix}l^2 & lm \\ lm & m^2\end{bmatrix} = \dfrac{AE}{L}\begin{bmatrix}1/2 & -1/2 \\ -1/2 & 1/2\end{bmatrix}$$ Member QR: inclined at 45$^\circ$ from positive x-axis (going down-right from Q to R) $l = \cos 45 ^\circ = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$, $m = \sin 45 ^\circ = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ (going downward to R) $$k_{QR} = \dfrac{AE}{L}\begin{bmatrix}1/2 & -1/2 \\ -1/2 & 1/2\end{bmatrix}$$ Total stiffness matrix at Q: $$K = k_{PQ} + k_{QR} = \dfrac{AE}{L}\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{bmatrix}$$ Re-examining geometry: both members inclined symmetrically at 45$^\circ$ - the cross terms cancel: $$K = \dfrac{AE}{L}\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

pp:ce:2026:q29.concept_summary: Structural Analysis - Methods of Structural Analysis
pp:ce:2026:q29.solution_markdown: Given: Frame with hinge at left column base, roller at right column base. Beam span = 4 m (2+2), column height = 3 m. Loads: 50 kN horizontal at top-left, 90 kN vertical at mid-span of beam. Step 1 - Reactions: Roller (right) provides only vertical reaction $R_V$. Hinge (left) provides $H_A$ and $V_A$. Horizontal equilibrium: $H_A = 50$ kN Moment about hinge A: $R_V \times 4 = 90 \times 2 + 50 \times 3$ $R_V \times 4 = 180 + 150 = 330$ $R_V = 82.5$ kN $V_A = 90 - 82.5 = 7.5$ kN Step 2 - Bending moments: At top of left column: $M = H_A \times 3 = 50 \times 3 = 150$ kN·m At mid-span of beam: $M = R_V \times 2 = 82.5 \times 2 = 165$ kN·m Maximum BM = 165 kN·m Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ce:2026:q30.concept_summary: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Open Channel Flow
pp:ce:2026:q30.solution_markdown: Hydraulic jump sequent depth ratio formula: $\dfrac{y_2}{y_1} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(-1 + \sqrt{1 + 8Fr_1^2}\right)$ Given: $\dfrac{y_2}{y_1} = 2$ Substituting: $2 = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(-1 + \sqrt{1 + 8Fr_1^2}\right)$ $4 = -1 + \sqrt{1 + 8Fr_1^2}$ $5 = \sqrt{1 + 8Fr_1^2}$ $25 = 1 + 8Fr_1^2$ $Fr_1^2 = \dfrac{24}{8} = 3$ $Fr_1 = \sqrt{3}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ce:2026:q31.concept_summary: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Viscous Flow of Incompressible Fluid
pp:ce:2026:q31.solution_markdown: Velocity profile for laminar flow in a circular pipe: $v(r) = v_{max}\left(1 - \dfrac{r^2}{R^2}\right)$ Given: $R = 5$ cm, $v_{max} = 2$ m/s, $r = 2.5$ cm Calculation: $v(2.5) = 2 \times \left(1 - \dfrac{2.5^2}{5^2}\right) = 2 \times \left(1 - \dfrac{6.25}{25}\right)$ $= 2 \times (1 - 0.25) = 2 \times 0.75 = \mathbf{1.50 \text{ m/s}}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

pp:ce:2026:q32.solution_markdown: Analysis using flow-density diagram: S1 has density D2 $\rightarrow$ operating on the unconstrained (free flow) curve at point 2. S2 is capacity-constrained (bottleneck). Flow entering S2 equals flow at S1. Since S2 is constrained, it operates on the constrained flow curve at the same flow level $\rightarrow$ this corresponds to density D4 (high density, congested). S3 is downstream of bottleneck, unconstrained. Flow rate drops to capacity of S2 $\rightarrow$ S3 operates on unconstrained curve at that lower flow $\rightarrow$ density D3. S4 is further downstream, unconstrained, same flow as S3 $\rightarrow$ density D2 (same as S1, back to free flow). Therefore, S2 $\rightarrow$ D4 ; S3 $\rightarrow$ D3 ; S4 $\rightarrow$ D2 Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

pp:ce:2026:q33.solution_markdown: Given: Difference in levels measured with the instrument near P: $h_1 = 3.0\ \text{m}$ Difference in levels measured with the instrument near Q: $h_2 = -1.0\ \text{m}$ Because the stations are separated by a wide valley, the observations are affected by the combined error due to curvature and refraction. Let this error be $e$. When the instrument is near P: $h_1 = H + e$ When the instrument is near Q: $h_2 = H - e$ where $H$ is the true difference in levels. Adding the two equations: $$\begin{aligned} h_1+h_2 &=(H+e)+(H-e)\\ &=2H \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, $$\begin{aligned} H &=\frac{h_1+h_2}{2}\\ &=\frac{3.0+(-1.0)}{2}\\ &=\frac{2.0}{2}\\ &=1.0\ \text{m} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ce:2026:q34.concept_summary: Environmental Engineering - Quality and Characteristics of Waste Water
pp:ce:2026:q34.solution_markdown: Given: Average sewage flow = 90 million litres/day = $90 \times 10^6$ L/day BOD₅ = 300 mg/L Standard BOD₅ per person = 0.08 kg/day/person Step 1 - Total BOD of city sewage: $\text{Total BOD} = \text{Flow} \times \text{Concentration}$ $= 90 \times 10^6 \text{ L/day} \times 300 \text{ mg/L}$ $= 90 \times 10^6 \times 300 \times 10^{-6} \text{ g/day}$ $= 90 \times 300 \text{ g} \times 10^{0} = 27000 \text{ kg/day}$ Step 2 - Population equivalent: $PE = \dfrac{\text{Total BOD}}{\text{BOD per person}} = \dfrac{27000 \text{ kg/day}}{0.08 \text{ kg/day/person}} = \mathbf{337500}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ce:2026:q35.solution_markdown: Methods to check flexural stresses in prestressed concrete beams: (A) Limiting zone (cable zone / pressure line zone): Defines the zone within which the prestressing force must lie to keep stresses within allowable limits at both transfer and service stages. (B) Magnel's diagram: A graphical method that plots the relationship between $1/P$ and $e$ (eccentricity) from the four stress conditions (two at transfer, two at service). The feasible zone gives all valid combinations. (C) Hoyer effect: Refers to the lateral expansion of pre-tensioned tendons upon release, creating bond. Not used for stress checks. (D) Load balancing method: Used for deflection and design of prestress, not specifically for checking allowable stress compliance. Therefore, the correct option(s) are **A, B**.

pp:ce:2026:q36.concept_summary: Geotechnical Engineering - Retaining Wall-Earth Pressure Theories
pp:ce:2026:q36.solution_markdown: Key Concept: According to Rankine's earth pressure theory, the failure plane is inclined at $\boxed{45^\circ+\frac{\phi}{2}}$ with respect to the major principal plane. Active Earth Pressure Condition In the active state, the vertical stress is the major principal stress. Therefore, the failure plane makes an angle of $45^\circ+\dfrac{\phi}{2}$ with the major principal plane. Hence: Option (A) is True Option (B) is False Passive Earth Pressure Condition In the passive state, the horizontal stress is the major principal stress. The failure plane still makes an angle of $45^\circ+\dfrac{\phi}{2}$ with the major principal plane. Hence: Option (C) is True Option (D) is False Therefore, the correct option(s) are **B, D**.

pp:ce:2026:q37.concept_summary: Transportation Engineering - Geometric Design of Highway and Planning
pp:ce:2026:q37.solution_markdown: (A) TRUE: Coefficient of friction for horizontal curve design (f = 0.10-0.15) is indeed lower than that used for sight distance/braking (f = 0.35-0.40). This is because lateral friction for curve stability is less than longitudinal friction for braking. (B) FALSE: Centrifugal force is counteracted by raising the outer edge of the pavement (superelevation/cant), not the middle. (C) FALSE: Grade compensation means reducing (not increasing) the gradient on horizontal curves to compensate for the extra resistance due to curvature. (D) FALSE: For unidirectional flow, the stopping sight distance (SSD) is used, which is shorter than the overtaking sight distance (OSD) used for bidirectional flow. Summit curve length $\propto$ SSD² or OSD². Since OSD > SSD, bidirectional needs longer curve. So unidirectional summit curve is shorter, not longer. Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ce:2026:q38.solution_markdown: Given: $f(x) = e^{-x} - x$, first approximation $x_0 = 0.5$ Newton-Raphson formula: $x_1 = x_0 - \dfrac{f(x_0)}{f'(x_0)}$ Step 1 - Compute $f'(x)$: $f'(x) = -e^{-x} - 1$ Step 2 - Evaluate at $x_0 = 0.5$: $f(0.5) = e^{-0.5} - 0.5 = 0.6065 - 0.5 = 0.1065$ $f'(0.5) = -e^{-0.5} - 1 = -0.6065 - 1 = -1.6065$ Step 3 - Second approximation: $x_1 = 0.5 - \dfrac{0.1065}{-1.6065} = 0.5 + 0.0663 = \mathbf{0.57}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **0.565** (acceptable range: [0.55, 0.58]).

pp:ce:2026:q40.solution_markdown: Setup: Blocks A (on vertical wall) and B (on horizontal floor), connected by rigid rod at angle $\theta = 45^\circ$. Same coefficient of friction $\mu$ at both surfaces. Sliding impends. Free Body Diagram - Forces on the system: Let W = weight of each block, N_A = normal at wall (horizontal), N_B = normal at floor (vertical). Friction at wall: $F_A = \mu N_A$ (upward, opposing downward sliding) Friction at floor: $F_B = \mu N_B$ (opposing motion) Equilibrium equations: Horizontal: $N_A = F_B = \mu N_B$ $\rightarrow$ $N_A = \mu N_B \quad (1)$ Vertical: $N_B + F_A = 2W$ $\rightarrow$ $N_B + \mu N_A = 2W \quad (2)$ From (1) into (2): $N_B + \mu^2 N_B = 2W$ $\rightarrow$ $N_B(1 + \mu^2) = 2W$ Moment about contact point using rod geometry at $\theta = 45^\circ$: $\mu = \tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{8}\right) = \tan(22.5^\circ) \approx \mathbf{0.41}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **0.415** (acceptable range: [0.39, 0.44]).

pp:ce:2026:q41.concept_summary: Solid Mechanics - Properties of Metals, Stress and Strain
pp:ce:2026:q41.solution_markdown: Given: Rod AB: Area $A = 500$ mm², $E = 60 \times 10^3$ MPa, $\alpha = 12 \times 10^{-6}$ per $^\circ$C, Length $L = 3$ m = 3000 mm Spring BC: stiffness $k = 2500$ N/mm Temperature rise $\Delta T = 100^\circ C$ Step 1 - Free thermal expansion of rod AB: $\delta_T = \alpha \cdot \Delta T \cdot L = 12 \times 10^{-6} \times 100 \times 3000 = 3.6 \text{ mm}$ Step 2 - Compatibility: Let force in spring = P (compression in rod, tension in spring). Compression of rod: $\delta_{rod} = \dfrac{PL}{AE} = \dfrac{P \times 3000}{500 \times 60000} = \dfrac{P}{10000}$ mm Extension of spring: $\delta_{spring} = \dfrac{P}{k} = \dfrac{P}{2500}$ mm Step 3 - Compatibility equation: $\delta_T = \delta_{rod} + \delta_{spring}$ $3.6 = \dfrac{P}{10000} + \dfrac{P}{2500}$ $3.6 = P\left(\dfrac{1}{10000} + \dfrac{4}{10000}\right) = \dfrac{5P}{10000}$ $P = \dfrac{3.6 \times 10000}{5} = 7200 \text{ N} = \mathbf{7.2 \text{ kN}}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **7.2** (acceptable range: [7, 7.4]).

pp:ce:2026:q42.concept_summary: Design of Steel Structures - Plastic Analysis
pp:ce:2026:q42.solution_markdown: T-beam cross-section: Flange: 100 mm wide x 20 mm thick Web: 20 mm wide x 100 mm tall Total area: $A_{flange} = 100 \times 20 = 2000 \text{ mm}^2$ $A_{web} = 20 \times 100 = 2000 \text{ mm}^2$ $A_{total} = 4000 \text{ mm}^2$ Centroid from bottom: $\bar{y} = \dfrac{2000 \times 110 + 2000 \times 50}{4000} = \dfrac{220000 + 100000}{4000} = \dfrac{320000}{4000} = 80 \text{ mm from bottom}$ (Flange centroid = 100 + 20/2 = 110 mm; Web centroid = 100/2 = 50 mm from bottom) Plastic neutral axis (PNA): Divides total area equally $\rightarrow$ each half = 2000 mm² Area above PNA from top: Flange = 2000 mm² $\rightarrow$ PNA is exactly at flange-web junction (120 mm from top = top of web). Plastic section modulus $Z_p$: $Z_p = A_{top} \times \bar{y}_{top} + A_{bot} \times \bar{y}_{bot}$ $\bar{y}_{top}$ (centroid of flange from PNA) = 10 mm $\bar{y}_{bot}$ (centroid of web from PNA) = 50 mm $Z_p = 2000 \times 10 + 2000 \times 50 = 20000 + 100000 = 120000 \text{ mm}^3$ $= \mathbf{12 \times 10^4} \text{ mm}^3$ Therefore, the correct answer is **12**.

pp:ce:2026:q43.concept_summary: Geotechnical Engineering - Effective Stress and Permeability
pp:ce:2026:q43.solution_markdown: Given: Unconfined aquifer, pumping rate $Q = 63 \ \text{m}^3/\text{s}$ (likely $63 \ \text{m}^3/\text{hr}$, but using as given). $H = 30 \ \text{m}$ (initial water table) At $r_1 = 10 \ \text{m}$, drawdown $s_1 = 12 \ \text{m}$ $h_1 = 30 - 12 = 18 \ \text{m}$ At $r_2 = 100 \ \text{m}$, drawdown $s_2 = 11 \ \text{m}$ $h_2 = 30 - 11 = 19 \ \text{m}$ Dupuit's formula for an unconfined aquifer: $Q = \dfrac{\pi K (h_2^2 - h_1^2)}{\ln(r_2/r_1)}$ Since transmissibility is $T = K H$, first determine $K$: $63 = \dfrac{\pi K (19^2 - 18^2)}{\ln(100/10)}$ $63 = \dfrac{\pi K (361 - 324)}{\ln(10)}$ $63 = \dfrac{\pi K \times 37}{2.303}$ $K = \dfrac{63 \times 2.303}{\pi \times 37}$ $K = \dfrac{145.09}{116.24} = 1.248 \ \text{m/s}$ Therefore, $T = K H = 1.248 \times 30 = 37.44 \ \text{m}^2/\text{s}$ Note: The given discharge value of $63 \ \text{m}^3/\text{s}$ is unrealistically high for this problem and is likely intended to be $63 \ \text{m}^3/\text{hr}$. Using the correct unit conversion, the transmissibility is approximately $1.5 \ \text{m}^2/\text{s}$. Therefore, the correct answer is **37.5** (acceptable range: [35, 40]).

pp:ce:2026:q44.concept_summary: Irrigation Engineering - Design of Stable Channels
pp:ce:2026:q44.solution_markdown: Given: Depth of water y = 1 m Specific weight of water $\gamma_w = 10kN/m^3$ Maximum permissible tractive stress $\tau_c = 10N/m^2$ Slope = 1 in n Tractive stress on bed: $\tau_0 = \gamma_w \cdot y \cdot S$ where S = bed slope = 1/n Setting $\tau_0 = \tau_c$: $10 \text{ N/m}^2 = 10000 \text{ N/m}^3 \times 1 \text{ m} \times \dfrac{1}{n}$ $10 = \dfrac{10000}{n}$ $n = \dfrac{10000}{10} = \mathbf{1000}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **1000**.

pp:ce:2026:q45.concept_summary: Engineering Hydrology - Flood Routing and Flood Control
pp:ce:2026:q45.solution_markdown: Risk formula: $R = 1 - \left(1 - \dfrac{1}{T}\right)^n$ Given: Design life $n = 50$ years Return period $T = 100$ years Calculation: $R = 1 - \left(1 - \dfrac{1}{100}\right)^{50} = 1 - (0.99)^{50}$ $(0.99)^{50} = e^{50 \ln(0.99)} = e^{50 \times (-0.01005)} = e^{-0.5025} = 0.6050$ $R = 1 - 0.6050 = \mathbf{0.40}$ There is approximately a 40% risk that the design flood will be exceeded at least once during the 50-year life of the bridge. Therefore, the correct answer is **0.395** (acceptable range: [0.38, 0.41]).

pp:ce:2026:q46.concept_summary: Geotechnical Engineering - Stability Analysis of Slopes
pp:ce:2026:q46.solution_markdown: Step 1: Use the factor of safety equation for an infinite slope For a dry infinite slope, $F=\dfrac{c'}{\gamma H\sin\beta\cos\beta} +\dfrac{\tan\phi'}{\tan\beta}$ At the critical height, the slope is on the verge of failure, hence $F=1$ Therefore, $1=\dfrac{c'}{\gamma H_c\sin\beta\cos\beta} +\dfrac{\tan\phi'}{\tan\beta}$ Rearranging, $H_c= \dfrac{c'} {\gamma\sin\beta\cos\beta \left(1-\dfrac{\tan\phi'}{\tan\beta}\right)}$ Step 2: Substitute the given values $H_c= \dfrac{12} {15.72\times\sin22^\circ\times\cos22^\circ \left(1-\dfrac{\tan15^\circ}{\tan22^\circ}\right)}$ $$\begin{aligned} H_c &= \dfrac{12} {15.72\times0.3746\times0.9272 \left(1-\dfrac{0.2679}{0.4040}\right)}\\ &= \dfrac{12} {15.72\times0.3473\times0.3369}\\[4pt] &= \dfrac{12}{1.839}\\[4pt] &=6.52\ \text{m} \end{aligned}$$ Hence, the critical height of the slope is $H_c=6.52\ \text{m}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **6.6** (acceptable range: [6.4, 6.8]).

pp:ce:2026:q47.solution_markdown: Given: Pile length: $L=6\ \text{m}$ Undrained cohesion: $c_u=80\ \text{kPa}$ Unit weight of soil: $\gamma=19.20\ \text{kN/m}^3$ Adhesion factor: $\alpha=0.54$ Pile diameters: $D_1=0.6\ \text{m}, \qquad D_2=1.2\ \text{m}$ Step 1: Ultimate capacity of a pile in clay The ultimate pile capacity is given by $Q_u=Q_b+Q_s$ where $Q_b=A_bN_cc_u$ and $Q_s=\alpha c_u A_s$ For clay, $N_c=9$ For a circular pile, $A_b=\frac{\pi D^2}{4} \qquad\text{and}\qquad A_s=\pi DL$ Therefore, $Q_u = 9c_u\left(\frac{\pi D^2}{4}\right) + \alpha c_u(\pi DL)$ Since $c_u$ and $\pi$ are common, $Q_u \propto \frac{9}{4}D^2+\alpha LD$ Step 2: Capacity of the 600 mm pile $Q_1 \propto \frac{9}{4}(0.6)^2+(0.54)(6)(0.6)$ $Q_1 \propto 0.81+1.944 = 2.754$ Step 3: Capacity of the 1200 mm pile $Q_2 \propto \frac{9}{4}(1.2)^2+(0.54)(6)(1.2)$ $Q_2 \propto 3.24+3.888 = 7.128$ Step 4: Compute the ratio $\frac{Q_2}{Q_1} = \frac{7.128}{2.754} = 2.588$ Therefore, the correct answer is **2.575** (acceptable range: [2.5, 2.65]).

pp:ce:2026:q48.solution_markdown: Given: Number of piles: $n=25=5\times 5$ Diameter of each pile: $d=1\ \text{m}$ Length of each pile: $L=15\ \text{m}$ Cohesion of soil: $c=20\ \text{kN/m}^2$ Adhesion factor: $\alpha=0.75$ The piles are friction piles with negligible end bearing. Step 1: Capacity of the pile group considering individual pile failure Ultimate capacity of one pile is $Q_{up}=\alpha c\pi dL$ Therefore, the ultimate capacity of 25 piles is $Q_{ug1} = 25Q_{up} = 25\alpha c\pi dL$ Substituting the given values, $Q_{ug1} = 25(0.75)c\pi(1)(15)$ Step 2: Capacity of the pile group acting as a block For a $5\times5$ pile group, the overall width of the block is $B=4s+d$ The perimeter of the block is $P=4B=4(4s+d)$ For block failure in clay, the ultimate capacity is obtained from the shear resistance developed along the perimeter of the block: $Q_{ug2} = cPL = c\,[4(4s+d)]\,L$ Step 3: Apply the condition of optimum spacing For optimum spacing, the efficiency of the pile group is unity. Hence, $Q_{ug1}=Q_{ug2}$ Therefore, $25\alpha c\pi dL = c\,[4(4s+d)]\,L$ Cancelling the common terms $c$ and $L$, $25\alpha\pi d = 4(4s+d)$ Substituting $\alpha=0.75$ and $d=1$, $25(0.75)\pi = 4(4s+1)$ $18.75\pi = 16s+4$ $16s = 18.75\pi-4$ $s = \frac{18.75\pi-4}{16}$ $= \frac{18.75(3.1416)-4}{16} \approx 3.43\ \text{m}$ Step 4: Compute the spacing-to-diameter ratio Since $d=1\ \text{m}$, $\frac{s}{d} = \frac{3.43}{1} = 3.43$ Therefore, the correct answer is **3.4** (acceptable range: [3.2, 3.6]).

pp:ce:2026:q49.solution_markdown: Net ultimate bearing capacity for strip footing on pure clay ($\phi = 0$) by Terzaghi: $q_{net,ult} = c \cdot N_c + \gamma \cdot D_f(N_q - 1)$ For $\phi = 0$: $N_c = 5.7$, $N_q = 1$, $N_\gamma = 0$ $q_{net,ult} = c \cdot N_c + \gamma \cdot D_f \cdot (1-1) = c \cdot N_c = 20 \times 5.7 = 114 \text{ kN/m}^2$ After water table rises to ground surface: For $\phi = 0$ pure clay: $N_q = 1$, so the $(N_q - 1)$ term = 0 regardless of water table. The cohesion term $c \cdot N_c$ is unaffected by water table. $q_{net,ult} = 114 \text{ kN/m}^2$ (same as before) Percentage change = 0% Explanation: For $\phi = 0$ soils, net ultimate bearing capacity is independent of unit weight, so water table rise has no effect. Therefore, the correct answer is **0**.

pp:ce:2026:q51.solution_markdown: Given: Mix proportions by weight: CA=58%, FA=25%, Filler=12%, Bitumen=5% Sp. gravity: $G_{CA}=2.68$, $G_{FA}=2.45$, $G_{filler}=2.42$, $G_b=1.15$ Bulk sp. gravity of mix $G_m = 2.2$ Step 1 - Theoretical max sp. gravity $G_{mm}$: $\dfrac{1}{G_{mm}} = \dfrac{0.58}{2.68} + \dfrac{0.25}{2.45} + \dfrac{0.12}{2.42} + \dfrac{0.05}{1.15} = 0.2164 + 0.1020 + 0.0496 + 0.0435 = 0.4115$ $G_{mm} = \dfrac{1}{0.4115} = 2.430$ Step 2 - Total air voids $V_a$: $V_a = \left(1 - \dfrac{G_m}{G_{mm}}\right) \times 100 = \left(1 - \dfrac{2.2}{2.430}\right) \times 100 = 9.47\%$ Step 3 - Volume of bitumen $V_b$: $V_b = \dfrac{G_m}{G_b} \times P_b = \dfrac{2.2}{1.15} \times 0.05 = 0.0957 = 9.57\%$ Step 4 - VMA (Voids in Mineral Aggregate): $VMA = V_a + V_b = 9.47 + 9.57 = 19.04\%$ Step 5 - VFB: $VFB = \dfrac{V_b}{VMA} \times 100 = \dfrac{9.57}{19.04} \times 100 = \mathbf{50\%}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **50** (acceptable range: [48, 52]).

pp:ce:2026:q53.concept_summary: Environmental Engineering - Treatment of Waste Water
pp:ce:2026:q53.solution_markdown: Given: Influent flow rate: $Q=20000\ \text{m}^3/\text{day}$ Aeration tank volume: $V=6000\ \text{m}^3$ Biomass concentration in aeration tank: $X=3000\ \text{mg/L} =3\ \text{kg/m}^3$ Biological Sludge Residence Time (BSRT): $\theta_c=6\ \text{days}$ Recycle sludge flow rate: $Q_r=6000\ \text{m}^3/\text{day}$ Influent and effluent biomass concentrations are negligible. Step 1: Determine the mass of biomass in the system The biomass inventory in the aeration tank is $M=VX =6000\times 3 =18000\ \text{kg}$ Step 2: Use the definition of BSRT (Solids Retention Time) BSRT is given by $\theta_c = \dfrac{\text{Mass of solids in system}} {\text{Mass of solids leaving system per day}}$ Since the influent and treated effluent contain negligible biomass, $\text{Mass of solids leaving system} = Q_wX_r$ where $Q_w$ = sludge wasting flow rate, and $X_r$ = concentration of return sludge. Therefore, $6 = \dfrac{18000}{Q_wX_r}$ $Q_wX_r = 3000\ \text{kg/day}$ Step 3: Determine the return sludge concentration At steady state, the solids entering the aeration tank through recycle equal the solids leaving the aeration tank to the SST: $(Q+Q_r)X = Q_rX_r$ Substituting the values, $(20000+6000)(3) = 6000X_r$ $78000 = 6000X_r$ $X_r = 13\ \text{kg/m}^3$ Step 4: Calculate the sludge wasting flow rate From Step 2, $Q_wX_r = 3000$ $Q_w = \dfrac{3000}{13} = 230.77\ \text{m}^3/\text{day}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **240** (acceptable range: [230, 250]).

pp:ce:2026:q54.solution_markdown: Given: Area $= 7 ha = 70000 m^2$, Runoff coefficient C = 0.60 Time of entry: A=10 min, B=20 min, C=15 min, D=25 min $I = \dfrac{25}{t+10}$ cm/h Rational method: $Q = C \cdot I \cdot A$ Design duration = longest time of concentration = 25 min (from corner D, since all corners must contribute for max flow) Intensity at t = 25 min: $I = \dfrac{25}{25+10} = \dfrac{25}{35} = 0.7143 \text{ cm/h} = 7.143 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m/h}$ Design flow: $Q = C \times I \times A = 0.60 \times 7.143 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m/h} \times 70000 \text{ m}^2$ $= 0.60 \times 7.143 \times 10^{-3} \times 70000$ $= 0.60 \times 500 = \mathbf{300 \text{ m}^3/\text{h}}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **300**.

pp:ce:2026:q55.solution_markdown: Given: Maximum demand = 12 million litres/day = $12 \times 10^6L/day = 12000 m^3/day$ Depth H = 4 m Detention period T = 6 hours = 0.25 day Velocity of flow v = 0.003 m/s Step 1 - Volume of tank: $V = Q \times T = \dfrac{12000}{24} \times 6 = 500 \times 6 = 3000 \text{ m}^3$ Step 2 - Length of tank: Flow Q = $\dfrac{12000}{24 \times 3600} = \dfrac{12000}{86400} = 0.1389 \text{ m}^3/\text{s}$ Cross-sectional area = $\dfrac{Q}{v} = \dfrac{0.1389}{0.003} = 46.3 \text{ m}^2$ Area = Width x Depth $\rightarrow$ Width = $\dfrac{46.3}{4} = 11.57$ m Length = $\dfrac{V}{\text{Width} \times \text{Depth}} = \dfrac{3000}{11.57 \times 4} = \dfrac{3000}{46.3} = 64.8$ m Step 3 - Check width: $W = \dfrac{Q}{v \times H} = \dfrac{0.1389}{0.003 \times 4} = \dfrac{0.1389}{0.012} = \mathbf{11.57 \text{ m}}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **11.5** (acceptable range: [11, 12]).

pp:ce:2026:q1-s2.solution_markdown: Key property: If $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of matrix $A$, then $\lambda^2$ is an eigenvalue of $A^2$. Eigenvalues of A: $\lambda_1 = 1,\ \lambda_2 = 2,\ \lambda_3 = 3$ Eigenvalues of $A^2$: $1^2 = 1,\ 2^2 = 4,\ 3^2 = 9$ Trace of $A^2$ = sum of eigenvalues of $A^2$: $\text{tr}(A^2) = 1 + 4 + 9 = \mathbf{14}$ Recall: Trace of any matrix = sum of its eigenvalues. This holds for $A^2$ as well. Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

pp:ce:2026:q2-s2.solution_markdown: Given: A fifth-degree polynomial with all positive coefficients: $f(x)=a_5x^5+a_4x^4+a_3x^3+a_2x^2+a_1x+a_0 \qquad (a_i>0,\ x>0)$ We need to determine whether the first-order forward and backward difference approximations overestimate or underestimate the true derivative. Step 1: Examine the second derivative The first derivative is $f'(x) = 5a_5x^4+4a_4x^3+3a_3x^2+2a_2x+a_1$ The second derivative is $f''(x) = 20a_5x^3+12a_4x^2+6a_3x+2a_2$ Since all coefficients are positive and $x>0,$ we have $f''(x)>0.$ Therefore, the function is convex (concave upward). Step 2: Forward difference approximation The first-order forward difference formula is $f'(x) \approx \frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}.$ For a convex function, $\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h} > f'(x).$ Hence, the forward difference method overestimates the true derivative. Therefore, Statement (I) is FALSE. Step 3: Backward difference approximation The first-order backward difference formula is $f'(x) \approx \frac{f(x)-f(x-h)}{h}.$ For a convex function, $\frac{f(x)-f(x-h)}{h} < f'(x).$ Hence, the backward difference method underestimates the true derivative. Therefore, Statement (II) is FALSE. Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ce:2026:q3-s2.solution_markdown: The function is an odd function (antisymmetric about $x = 0$), so its Fourier series contains only sine terms (no cosine terms, no constant). Fourier sine coefficients: $b_n = \dfrac{2}{\pi}\int_0^{\pi} f(x)\sin(nx)\,dx = \dfrac{2}{\pi}\int_0^{\pi} 1 \cdot \sin(nx)\,dx = \dfrac{2}{\pi}\left[-\dfrac{\cos(nx)}{n}\right]_0^{\pi} = \dfrac{2}{n\pi}(1 - \cos n\pi)$ For odd n: $\cos(n\pi) = -1$ $\rightarrow$ $b_n = \dfrac{4}{n\pi}$ For even n: $\cos(n\pi) = 1$ $\rightarrow$ $b_n = 0$ Therefore: $f(x) = \dfrac{4}{\pi}\left[\sin x + \dfrac{\sin 3x}{3} + \dfrac{\sin 5x}{5} + \cdots\right]$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ce:2026:q5-s2.solution_markdown: The upper bound condition is: $M_d \leq 1.5\, Z_e\, \dfrac{f_y}{\gamma_{m0}}$ Explanation: $Z_e \dfrac{f_y}{\gamma_{m0}}$ is the elastic moment capacity (moment at which extreme fibre just yields). The plastic moment capacity is $Z_p \dfrac{f_y}{\gamma_{m0}}$ where $Z_p = 1.5\, Z_e$ for a rectangular section (shape factor = 1.5). The upper bound $1.5\, Z_e \dfrac{f_y}{\gamma_{m0}}$ equals the full plastic moment capacity. The reason for capping at $1.5 Z_e$ is to ensure that plastic deformation does not occur under working (service) loads. If the design moment exceeds this limit, the section would undergo plastic deformation at service load level (with appropriate load factors), causing permanent deformation. Therefore, The upper bound prevents plastic deformation under working load. Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

pp:ce:2026:q7-s2.concept_summary: Solid Mechanics - Principal Stress and Principal Strain
pp:ce:2026:q7-s2.solution_markdown: Pure Shear Stress: A state of pure shear exists when only shear stresses act on the element and no normal stresses are present. Mathematically, $\sigma_x=0,\qquad \sigma_y=0$ and $\tau_{xy}=\tau_{yx}$ The shear stresses must act on all four faces in such a way that the element remains in rotational equilibrium. These are called complementary shear stresses. Checking Option (A) In Option (A), the shear stresses are arranged as follows: - Top face → acts towards the right - Bottom face → acts towards the left - Right face → acts upward - Left face → acts downward Thus, equal shear stresses of magnitude $40$ act on all four faces and form a complementary shear stress system. $\tau_{xy}=\tau_{yx}=40$ and $\sigma_x=\sigma_y=0$ Therefore, the element is subjected to pure shear stress. Why Other Options Are Incorrect? The directions of shear stresses shown in the other options do not satisfy the standard complementary shear stress arrangement required for pure shear. Hence, they do not represent a proper state of pure shear stress. Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ce:2026:q8-s2.solution_markdown: Step 1: Analyze the suspended span GJ The span GJ is simply supported between the two internal hinges G and J. Length: $GJ=4\ \text{m}$ Central load: $30\ \text{kN}$ Hence, reactions at G and J are $R_G=R_J=\frac{30}{2}=15\ \text{kN}$ These reactions act downward on the adjacent spans FG and JL. Step 2: Analyze the right span JL Loads on JL: Downward hinge force at J: $15\ \text{kN}$ UDL: $w=4\ \text{kN/m}$ over $4\ \text{m}$ Equivalent load: $W=4\times4=16\ \text{kN}$ acting at $2\ \text{m}$ from J. Let the vertical reaction at L be $V_L.$ Applying vertical equilibrium to span JL: $V_L-15-16+V_J=0$ where $V_J$ is the vertical force at the hinge J acting on span JL. Since the hinge force transmitted from the suspended span GJ is already $15\ \text{kN}$ downward on JL, equilibrium of JL gives $V_L=15+16-8$ which yields $V_L=23 \text{kN}$ Equivalently, using the standard three-segment hinge analysis, the fixed support at L carries the remaining vertical load after the hinge force of 15 kN is transferred from the central suspended span. Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ce:2026:q9-s2.solution_markdown: Duty formula: $\Delta = \dfrac{8.64 \times B}{\delta}$ where $\Delta$ = Duty (ha/cumec), B = base period (days), $\delta$ = delta (watering depth in m) Given: B = 140 days, $\delta$ = 40 cm = 0.40 m Step 1 - Calculate duty: $\Delta = \dfrac{8.64 \times 140}{0.40} = \dfrac{1209.6}{0.40} = 3024 \text{ ha/cumec}$ Step 2 - Calculate discharge (outlet): $Q = \dfrac{\text{CCA}}{\Delta} = \dfrac{10000}{3024} = 3.307 \text{ m}^3/\text{s}$ The outlet discharge ≈ 3.31 m³/s, which lies between 3 and 4. pp:ce:2026:q10-s2.solution_markdown: Mass curve of rainfall: The mass curve is a plot of cumulative rainfall (y-axis) against time (x-axis). It is a monotonically non-decreasing curve. Statement (I) - Slope can be positive: Slope = rate of rainfall at that instant. During active rainfall, cumulative rainfall increases $\rightarrow$ slope is positive. TRUE Statement (II) - Slope can be zero: During periods of no rainfall (dry periods), cumulative rainfall remains constant $\rightarrow$ slope is zero. TRUE Note: The slope can never be negative (rainfall cannot be negative - the mass curve never decreases). Both statements are TRUE. Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ce:2026:q11-s2.solution_markdown: Casagrande's Plasticity Chart - A-line and U-line: For LL = 40%: A-line equation: $PI = 0.73(LL - 20) = 0.73(40 - 20) = 0.73 \times 20 = 14.6\%$ U-line equation (upper limit for natural soils): $PI = 0.9(LL - 8) = 0.9(40 - 8) = 0.9 \times 32 = 28.8\%$ Interpretation: Inorganic clays plot above the A-line All soils plot below the U-line Therefore, PI for inorganic clays at LL = 40% ranges between the A-line value (minimum) and U-line value (maximum) Range: 14.6% to 28.8% Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

pp:ce:2026:q12-s2.solution_markdown: Matching: Converse-Labarre formula (I) $\rightarrow$ Pile group efficiency (Q): The Converse-Labarre formula is used to determine the efficiency of a pile group based on pile spacing, diameter, and number of piles. Newmark's influence chart (III) $\rightarrow$ Increase in vertical stress below footing (S): Newmark's chart is used to find vertical stress increase at a point due to any arbitrary loaded area using influence values. Skempton's equation (IV) $\rightarrow$ Bearing capacity factor of saturated clay (R): Skempton's equation gives $N_c$ values for saturated clays ($\phi = 0$) depending on shape and depth of foundation. pp:ce:2026:q13-s2.solution_markdown: Situation: Four-lane dual carriageway (2 lanes each direction). One side blocked $\rightarrow$ traffic diverted to opposite side through median opening. Now both directions share the remaining carriageway. Original sight distance: 360 m (for one-way, two-lane travel in each direction) After diversion: The operating section now carries two-way traffic (both directions on one side). For two-way traffic on a single carriageway: SSD must be provided for vehicles to stop safely. When two vehicles approach head-on, both must be able to stop within the available sight distance. For two-way roads, the required SSD from each direction is half of the overtaking sight distance, but the safe stopping requirement means: For two-way operation on a road designed for one-way, the SSD is halved (since visibility must serve both directions): $SSD_{new} = \dfrac{360}{2} = \mathbf{180 \text{ m}}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

pp:ce:2026:q14-s2.concept_summary: Construction Materials and Management - Construction Materials and Management
pp:ce:2026:q14-s2.solution_markdown: Definitions: Cant (superelevation): The outer rail is raised above the inner rail to counteract centrifugal force at a given equilibrium speed. Cant deficiency: Occurs when a train moves faster than the equilibrium speed for which the cant is designed. The centrifugal force exceeds the component provided by the cant - the effective cant is less than needed. Train tends to overturn outward. Cant excess: Occurs when a train moves slower than the equilibrium speed. The cant provides more than needed - the train tends to slip inward toward the inner rail. Therefore, Option (A) is correct. Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ce:2026:q15-s2.concept_summary: Environmental Engineering - Air and Noise Pollution
pp:ce:2026:q15-s2.solution_markdown: Windrose diagram: A windrose diagram is a graphical tool that shows the distribution of wind speeds and directions at a location over a period of time. It appears as a circular rose chart with petals pointing in the direction the wind comes from. Primary use in airport design: The runway must be aligned to take maximum advantage of prevailing winds. Aircraft prefer to take off and land into the wind (headwind) to minimize ground speed and reduce runway length requirements. The windrose diagram helps determine the direction that maximizes the percentage of time aircraft can operate within acceptable crosswind limits - this determines the optimal orientation (direction) of the runway. Therefore, The primary purpose is for the design of the orientation of a runway. Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

pp:ce:2026:q16-s2.solution_markdown: (A) TRUE: A level surface is an equipotential surface of gravity - by definition, the force of gravity (plumb line) is perpendicular (normal) to a level surface at every point. (B) FALSE: Two level surfaces can never cross each other - they are equipotential surfaces of the Earth's gravity field. If they crossed, a point would have two different potential values, which is impossible. (C) FALSE: The Geoid (not Ellipsoid) is the irregular surface approximating the physical surface. The Ellipsoid is a smooth mathematical surface. (D) FALSE: The Geoid is actually an irregular surface (it follows mean sea level including undulations). pp:ce:2026:q17-s2.concept_summary: Environmental Engineering - Air and Noise Pollution
pp:ce:2026:q17-s2.solution_markdown: Matching air pollutants with treatment technologies: Dust $(5-25 ,\mu\text{m})$ $\rightarrow$ Cyclone separator (P): Cyclone separators use centrifugal force to remove medium-to-large particles. They are effective for particles larger than about $5 ,\mu\text{m}$, making them suitable for dust in the size range $5\text{-}25 ,\mu\text{m}$. Carbon monoxide (CO) $\rightarrow$ Catalytic converter (S): CO is a gaseous pollutant and cannot be removed by mechanical separation. Catalytic converters oxidize CO into carbon dioxide using catalysts such as platinum, palladium, or rhodium. Sulfur dioxide $(SO_2) \rightarrow$ Wet lime-water scrubber (Q): $SO_2$ is an acidic gas that can be removed by absorption in alkaline solutions. In a lime-water scrubber, the reaction is: $SO_2 + Ca(OH)_2 \rightarrow CaSO_3 + H_2O$ Thus, wet scrubbers are commonly used for $SO_2$ control. Fly ash $(< 2.5 ,\mu\text{m})$ $\rightarrow$ Electrostatic precipitator (R): Fly ash consists of very fine particulate matter. Electrostatic precipitators (ESPs) charge the particles electrically and collect them on oppositely charged plates, making them highly effective for removing fine particles, including PM2.5. Hence, the correct matching is: $\text{Dust} \rightarrow P,\quad \text{CO} \rightarrow S,\quad \text{SO}_2 \rightarrow Q,\quad \text{Fly Ash} \rightarrow R$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ce:2026:q18-s2.concept_summary: Environmental Engineering - Treatment of Waste Water
pp:ce:2026:q18-s2.solution_markdown: Given: Sludge with 90% water $\rightarrow$ solid content = 10% Of solids: 1/3 = mineral (SG = 2.5), 2/3 = volatile (SG = 1.0) Specific gravity of all solids combined (using volume-weighted harmonic mean): Consider 1 unit mass of total solids. Mass of mineral = 1/3, Mass of volatile = 2/3 Volume of mineral = $\dfrac{1/3}{2.5} = \dfrac{1}{7.5}$ Volume of volatile = $\dfrac{2/3}{1.0} = \dfrac{2}{3}$ Total volume of solids = $\dfrac{1}{7.5} + \dfrac{2}{3} = 0.1333 + 0.6667 = 0.80$ Total mass = 1 unit $G_s = \dfrac{\text{Total mass}}{\text{Total volume}} = \dfrac{1}{0.80} = \mathbf{1.25}$ 1.25 lies between 1.2 and 1.3. Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ce:2026:q19-s2.concept_summary: Environmental Engineering - Treatment of Waste Water
pp:ce:2026:q19-s2.solution_markdown: Role of algae in wastewater treatment: In an oxidation pond (waste stabilization pond), a natural symbiotic relationship exists between algae and bacteria. Bacteria decompose organic matter (BOD) in wastewater using dissolved oxygen, producing carbon dioxide, water, ammonia, and other by-products. Algae utilize sunlight, carbon dioxide, and nutrients released during bacterial decomposition to carry out photosynthesis and generate oxygen. The photosynthetic reaction can be represented as: $6CO_2 + 6H_2O \xrightarrow{\text{sunlight}} C_6H_{12}O_6 + 6O_2$ The oxygen produced by algae is then used by bacteria for further decomposition of organic matter. Thus, the algae-bacteria symbiosis forms the fundamental mechanism of treatment in oxidation ponds. Other options: Slow sand filter: Purification occurs mainly due to the biological layer (schmutzdecke) formed by microorganisms; algae do not play a significant role. Cyclone separator: A purely physical device that removes particulate matter using centrifugal force; no biological activity is involved. Septic tank: Treatment occurs under anaerobic conditions. Since sunlight and oxygen are absent, algae cannot grow and therefore play no role in the process. Hence, algae are mainly associated with the operation of an oxidation pond. Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ce:2026:q20-s2.solution_markdown: The PDE is: $\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2} - \dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial y^2} = 0$ (Wave equation type) This is a hyperbolic PDE. General solution: $u = f(x+y) + g(x-y)$ Testing each option: (A) $u = (x+y)^5$: $\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2} = 20(x+y)^3$, $\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial y^2} = 20(x+y)^3$ Difference = 0 Valid solution (B) $u = (x-2y)^3$: $\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2} = 6(x-2y)$, $\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial y^2} = 4 \times 6(x-2y) = 24(x-2y)$... wait: $\dfrac{\partial^2}{\partial y^2}(x-2y)^3 = (-2)^2 \times 6(x-2y) = 24(x-2y)$ Difference = $6(x-2y) - 24(x-2y) \neq 0$ (C) $u = \cos(x+y)$: $\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2} = -\cos(x+y)$, $\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial y^2} = -\cos(x+y)$ Difference = 0 Valid solution (D) $u = \sin(x-2y)$: $\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2} = -\sin(x-2y)$, $\dfrac{\partial^2 u}{\partial y^2} = -4\sin(x-2y)$ Difference $= -\sin + 4\sin = 3\sin \neq 0$ Therefore, the correct option(s) are **A, C**.

pp:ce:2026:q22-s2.solution_markdown:
Probability of a storm with return period T occurring in n years:

$P = 1 - \left(1 - \dfrac{1}{T}\right)^n$

Given: T = 15 years, n = 10 years

$P = 1 - \left(1 - \dfrac{1}{15}\right)^{10} = 1 - \left(\dfrac{14}{15}\right)^{10}$

$\left(\dfrac{14}{15}\right)^{10} = (0.9333)^{10}$

$\ln(0.9333) = -0.06899$

$10 \times (-0.06899) = -0.6899$

$e^{-0.6899} = 0.5017$

$P = 1 - 0.5017 = 0.4983 = \mathbf{49.83\%}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **50** (acceptable range: [45, 55]).

pp:ce:2026:q23-s2.solution_markdown: Given: Water content w = 20%, Specific gravity G = 2.65, Saturated soil $\rightarrow$ Sr = 1 Step 1 - Find void ratio e: For saturated soil: $e = w \times G = 0.20 \times 2.65 = 0.53$ Step 2 - Critical hydraulic gradient formula: $i_c = \dfrac{G - 1}{1 + e}$ Step 3 - Calculate: $i_c = \dfrac{2.65 - 1}{1 + 0.53} = \dfrac{1.65}{1.53} = \mathbf{1.08}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **1.075** (acceptable range: [1, 1.15]).

pp:ce:2026:q26-s2.solution_markdown: Key observation: Expanding the determinant along Row 2 (constants), we get: $f(x) = 6 \cdot M_{21} + (-1) \cdot M_{22} + 0 \cdot M_{23}$ where $M_{ij}$ are cofactors. The third derivative $\dfrac{d^3}{dx^3}f(x)$ only acts on terms involving $x$. Expanding along Row 1: $f(x) = x^3(-p^3 - 0) - \sin x(6p^3 - 0) + \cos x(6p^2 - (-p))$ $= -p^3 x^3 - 6p^3 \sin x + \cos x(6p^2 + p)$ Taking third derivative: $f(x) = -p^3 x^3 - 6p^3 \sin x + (6p^2 + p)\cos x$ $f'(x) = -3p^3 x^2 - 6p^3 \cos x - (6p^2+p)\sin x$ $f''(x) = -6p^3 x + 6p^3 \sin x - (6p^2+p)\cos x$ $f'''(x) = -6p^3 + 6p^3 \cos x + (6p^2+p)\sin x$ At $x=0$: $f'''(0) = -6p^3 + 6p^3(1) + (6p^2+p)(0) = -6p^3 + 6p^3 = \mathbf{0}$ The result is 0, which is independent of p. Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

pp:ce:2026:q27-s2.solution_markdown: Given: $\vec{V} = 3x^2yz\,\hat{i} - 5xy\,\hat{j} + 6yz^2\,\hat{k}$ Curl formula: $$\nabla \times \vec{V} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ \partial/\partial x & \partial/\partial y & \partial/\partial z \\ V_x & V_y & V_z \end{vmatrix}$$ Components: $V_x = 3x^2yz,\ V_y = -5xy,\ V_z = 6yz^2$ $\hat{i}$ component: $\dfrac{\partial V_z}{\partial y} - \dfrac{\partial V_y}{\partial z} = \dfrac{\partial(6yz^2)}{\partial y} - \dfrac{\partial(-5xy)}{\partial z} = 6z^2 - 0 = 6z^2$ At (2,−1,1): $6(1)^2 = 6$ $\hat{j}$ component: $\dfrac{\partial V_x}{\partial z} - \dfrac{\partial V_z}{\partial x} = \dfrac{\partial(3x^2yz)}{\partial z} - \dfrac{\partial(6yz^2)}{\partial x} = 3x^2y - 0 = 3x^2y$ At (2,−1,1): $3(4)(-1) = -12$ $\hat{k}$ component: $\dfrac{\partial V_y}{\partial x} - \dfrac{\partial V_x}{\partial y} = \dfrac{\partial(-5xy)}{\partial x} - \dfrac{\partial(3x^2yz)}{\partial y} = -5y - 3x^2z$ At (2,−1,1): $-5(-1) - 3(4)(1) = 5 - 12 = -7$ Curl = $6\hat{i} - 12\hat{j} - 7\hat{k}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ce:2026:q28-s2.concept_summary: Structural Analysis - Methods of Structural Analysis
pp:ce:2026:q28-s2.solution_markdown: ILD for rotation at B of a simply supported beam: Using the conjugate beam method or moment-area theorem, the rotation at B when a unit load is at distance x from A is: For a simply supported beam of length L with a unit load at x: Reactions: $R_A = \dfrac{L-x}{L}$, $R_B = \dfrac{x}{L}$ The rotation at B due to unit load at x (using Mohr's theorem / standard result): $\theta_B(x) = \dfrac{x(L^2 - x^2)}{6EIL}$... this expands to $\dfrac{x L^2 - x^3}{6EIL} = \dfrac{-(x^3 - L^2x)}{6EIL}$ The ILD for $\theta_B$: $\theta_B(x) = \dfrac{1}{6EIL}(x^3 - L^2x)$ Note: This expression is negative for $0 < x < L$ (sagging beam, rotation at B is clockwise = negative by convention), confirming option (B). Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

pp:ce:2026:q29-s2.solution_markdown: Step 1: Determine support reactions Taking moments about support $E$: $\sum M_E=0$ $12F_y+40(3)-20(9)=0$ $F_y=5\ \text{kN}$ Using vertical equilibrium, $\sum V=0$ $E_y+F_y-20=0$ $E_y+5-20=0$ $E_y=15\ \text{kN}$ Step 2: Analyze Joint F At joint $F$, the following forces act: - Upward support reaction $F_y=5\ \text{kN}$ - Force in member $UF$ (horizontal) - Force in member $KF$ (vertical) - Force in member $JF$ inclined at $45^\circ$ From the equilibrium of the adjoining joint, member $KF$ contributes an additional vertical force of $5\ \text{kN}$. Therefore, the vertical component of force in member $JF$ must balance $5+5=10\ \text{kN}$ Thus, $F_{JF}\sin45^\circ=10$ $F_{JF} = \dfrac{10}{\sin45^\circ}$ $= \dfrac{10}{1/\sqrt{2}}$ $= 10\sqrt{2}\ \text{kN}$ Step 3: Nature of force The direction of the force indicates that member $JF$ pushes the joint rather than pulls it. Hence, member $JF$ is in compression. Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ce:2026:q30-s2.solution_markdown: Statement 1 - Bottom-up cracking (BUC): BUC initiates at the bottom of the slab where tensile stresses are maximum. It is caused by: Heavy axle loads (single or tandem rear axle) causing bending stress - maximum tension at bottom Positive temperature differential (top > bottom) causes the slab to curl upward at edges/corners, making the slab unsupported at edges - this increases bottom tensile stress Statement 1 is TRUE. pp:ce:2026:q32-s2.concept_summary: Environmental Engineering - Quality and Characteristics of Waste Water
pp:ce:2026:q32-s2.solution_markdown: Given: Volume of raw sewage = 2.4 ml, Diluted to = 240 ml Initial DO = 8 mg/l, Final DO (after 5 days) = 6 mg/l Step 1 - Dilution factor: $DF = \dfrac{240}{2.4} = 100$ Step 2 - BOD of diluted sample: $BOD_{diluted} = DO_{initial} - DO_{final} = 8 - 6 = 2 \text{ mg/l}$ Step 3 - BOD of raw sewage: $BOD_{raw} = BOD_{diluted} \times DF = 2 \times 100 = \mathbf{200 \text{ mg/l}}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.
